Thanks, Ben / Jordan —

I've reviewed Acme's redlines and pulled a short summary of the material items for Redwood negotiators. See attached: Redline_Summary_Redwood_20250716.pdf. High-level notes below.

Key Redwood positions / questions:
1) Data processing & deletion — Acme's requested deletion timeline (within 7 days) is aggressive. Proposed compromise: 30 days for non-production logs and 45 days for backup snapshots; 7 days for customer-controlled uploads on hosted if requested. Need confirmation from infra (Dev) whether 30/45 is operationally feasible for the environments Acme expects to use.

2) Liability cap — Acme requests unlimited liability carve-outs for breaches tied to customer data. Redwood standard is a $X per-incident / $Y aggregate cap tied to fees. Proposed negotiation posture: maintain capped liability with carve-outs only for willful misconduct.

3) Subprocessors — we'll provide the current subprocessor list and agree to notify of material changes; Acme asks for prior consent for new subprocessors. Suggest we offer notice + objection window (30 days) rather than prior consent to preserve operational flexibility.

4) Termination for convenience (Order Form) — Acme requests 60-day notice; acceptable to Redwood, provided fees for committed Dedicated capacity are handled via prorated refunds or buyouts. Finance needs to confirm.

Action items:
- Dev: confirm deletion timelines for pinned private deployments and hosted retention behaviors. (Dev, can you comment inline in Drive by EOD?)
- Jordan: propose intake call times to Acme.
- Jordan / Stephanie: we'll draft an MSA addendum that captures the region pinning and suggested compromise language for liability and subprocessors.

I'll be on the 10:00 PT intake call if scheduled.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
